query: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi has high saturation magnetization but a low coercive field, and reported single-phase fcc high-entropy alloys derived from it have coercive fields no greater than 100 Oe in the reported magnetic measurements. What single intervention could overcome this coercivity limitation? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted change relative to single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a matched derivative, the relevant compositional, structural, and measurement boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing controlled Al doping (up to ~10 at%) into single-phase fcc FeCoNi, followed by solution treatment and aging to form B2-type nanoprecipitates, will pin domain walls and thereby increase the coercive field beyond the ~100 Oe limit while maintaining high saturation magnetization.
generation.material_initial_state: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a closely related derivative with coercivity ~100 Oe and high saturation magnetization.
generation.intervention: Add 5–10 at% Al and perform solution treatment at ~1100 °C followed by aging at 600–700 °C to induce B2 nanoprecipitation.
generation.conditions: FeCoNi-based alloy with 5–10 at% Al, solution-treated at ~1100 °C and aged for up to 10 hours in the 600–700 °C range, with magnetic characterization at room temperature.
generation.structural_mediator: Nanoprecipitates of B2 phase dispersed within the fcc matrix.
generation.mechanism: The B2 nanoprecipitates act as strong pinning centers, thereby increasing resistance to domain wall motion and enhancing coercivity.
generation.predicted_outcome: Coercivity will exceed 200 Oe, with only modest reduction in saturation magnetization compared to the undoped single-phase fcc FeCoNi baseline.
generation.baseline: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi alloys or derivatives with typical coercivity at or below ~100 Oe.
generation.boundary: The effect holds for Al additions up to ~10 at% and requires appropriate heat treatment. Excessive Al content or altered processing routes could degrade mechanical or magnetic properties.
generation.uncertainty: Optimal Al content and heat treatment parameters are not fully constrained and require additional experimental exploration to confirm maximum coercivity gains.

falsification_experiment.design: Arc-melt FeCoNi-based alloys containing 1–10 at% Al. Homogenize at ~1100 °C, water-quench, age at 600–700 °C for systematic durations, then characterize phase formation by XRD/TEM and measure hysteresis loops via VSM at room temperature.
measurements: Amount and morphology of B2 precipitates (XRD/TEM)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if B2 precipitates are not observed after aging or if coercivity remains at ≤100 Oe under these doping and heat-treatment conditions.

cited_evidence.text:
Alloy ingots with a nominal composition of Al x CoCrFeNi ( x = 0.1, 0.75 and 1.5) were synthesized by arc-melting a mixture of pure metals (purity >99.6 wt.%) in a Ti-gettered high-purity argon atmosphere. These ingots were remelted at least four times to ensure chemical homogeneity. Melted alloys were eventually drop-cast into a mold Φ 5 × 70 mm 3 . The solidified ingots were cut into thin pieces 1 mm thick and one side polished. The sample densities for x = 0.1, 0.75 and 1.5, which were measured by Archimedes method, are 8.1, 7.4 and 6.9 g·cm −3 , respectively. The microstructures of as-prepared Al x CoCrFeNi HEAs ( x = 0.1, 0.75 and 1.5) are single fcc, fcc plus ordered bcc (B2) and B2 plus disordered bcc (A2), respectively. The XRD and SEM characterization results are given in Supplementary Figs S2 and S3 , the detailed microstructure characterizations can be also found in our previous study [14] .

The microstructure and compositions of as-prepared Al x CoCrFeNi HEAs were first characterized by XRD (Philips X Pert Pro), SEM (FEI, Nano430) and TEM (FEI, Tecnai F30). TEM samples were prepared by mechanical polishing to approximately 100 μm thickness, followed by dual jet polishi

While the AlCoFeNi high entropy alloy exhibits a single ordered B2 phase at high temperature, both the substitution of ferromagnetic Co with antiferromagnetic Cr, and lower annealing temperatures lead to a tendency for this system to decompose into a two-phase mixture of ordered B2 and disordered BCC solid solution. The length scale of this decomposition is determined by the combination of composition and annealing temperature, as demonstrated in this investigation by comparing and contrasting AlCoFeNi with the AlCo 0.5 Cr 0.5 FeNi alloy. The resulting phase stability has been rationalized based on solution thermodynamic predictions. Additionally, it is shown that replacement of Co by Cr in the AlCoFeNi alloy resulted in a substantial reduction in saturation magnetization and increase in coercivity. The microhardness is also strongly influenced by the composition and the length scale of B2 + BCC decomposition in these high entropy alloys.
